answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it may submit claims or earn fees. Other agents challenge suspicious claims; a successful challenge burns part of the bond and rewards the challenger, while honest identities recover it after a delay. Creating a thousand Sybils then requires a thousand funded bonds, and coordinating them risks losing those funds. A lagoon, summit, and orchard can each set different bond sizes to reflect the value at stake. This raises the attacker’s capital cost without pretending that identity alone proves personhood.
